method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs
why_not_one_block_off: PRINTED NAME. The corridor is lettered 'AVENUE K.' vertically inside the roadway I measured on both plates - sheet 56 at native x~2198 (east side of view 2, west side of view 3) and sheet 62 at native x~2177 (east side of view 2, west side of view 3). Unlike its neighbours it carries no alternative street name, which is itself part of the identification: Ave J is always lettered 'AVE. J. OR BROADWAY' and Ave L 'AVENUE L.'. HUNDRED-BLOCK BREAK. On BOTH sheets Ave K is the 1000/1100 break of the numbered-street addresses. Sheet 56: the column WEST of it reads 1001 1003 1005 1007 1009 1011 1013 1015 1017 1019 1021 1023 along 29TH ST and 1002 1004 ... 1024 along 30TH ST (blocks 148, 149); the column EAST of it reads 1101 1103 1105 1107 1109 1111 1113 1115 1117 1119 1121 1123 / 1102 1104 ... 1124 (blocks 88, 89). Sheet 62: the column WEST reads 1001 1003 ... 1023 / 1002 1004 ... 1024 along 30TH and 31ST ST (blocks 150, 151) and the column EAST reads 1101 1103 ... 1123 / 1102 1104 ... 1124 (blocks 90, 91, the latter containing the 3rd District Goliad Public Free School). Same 1000-block west face and 1100-block east face on both plates. ONE BLOCK WEST EXCLUDED. That corridor is lettered 'AVE. J. OR BROADWAY' on both plates (sheet 56 centre native 1152.9, sheet 62 centre native 1129.2, about 1046 px west) and it is the 900/1000 break, not the 1000/1100 break - the 921 923 / 922 924 run is printed on its west face on both sheets. It is also drafted much wider than a normal avenue: 303.0 native px between facing block lines on sheet 56 and 302.6 on sheet 62 (about 100 ft), versus 212.6 and 212.7 px (about 70 ft) for Ave K, and sheet 62 letters '150 ft wide' beside it. So the two cannot be confused. ONE BLOCK EAST EXCLUDED. That corridor is lettered 'AVENUE L.' on both plates (sheet 56 centre native ~3201, sheet 62 centre native ~3175, about 1000 px east, both near the sheets' east borders) and it is the 1100/1200 break - the whole 1101-1124 run lies BETWEEN Ave K and Ave L, so Ave L cannot be the 1000/1100 line. NOT MATCHED BY MOSAIC PROXIMITY AND NOT BY EQUAL NATIVE X. The identification above rests only on the lettering and the address runs. It happens that these two plates are nearly co-registered in native x already (shift about -22 px, far less than the ~1025 px one-block scale), but that was the OUTPUT of the identification, not an input: I read the corridor names and the 1000/1100 runs on each sheet independently before comparing coordinates. The candidate lists offered (56: 846/1817/2789, 62: 2710/1653/596) were not used to choose the corridor. CORROBORATION. Two independently measured lettered avenues give the same plate-to-plate x shift: Ave K 2176.6-2198.5 = -21.9 px and Ave J (Broadway) 1129.2-1152.9 = -23.7 px, agreeing to 1.8 px, where a one-block error would be about 1025 px. Internal lattice check on sheet 56: mid-block 20-ft alleys sit at native centres 604.0, 1698.5 and 2701.0, i.e. one alley per block column, with Broadway centred at 1151 between the first two and Ave K at 2199 between the last two; the alley-to-alley span is 1002.5 px across Ave K but 1094.5 px across Broadway, the 92 px difference being exactly the extra width Broadway is drafted with. Alleys measure only ~60 native px (20 ft) against the avenue's ~212 px (70 ft), so no alley was taken for an avenue. Stacking confirmed: sheet 56's bottom margin prints '62', sheet 62's top margin prints '56', and 30TH ST is the shared seam (bottom row of 56, top row of 62). NOTE ON THE RED MARKER. The red line in each crop is only the crop centre (native 832 / 1664 / 2495); on these plates it lands mid-block every time. The reported values are roadway centrelines - the midpoint of the two facing block lines - measured against the native pixel grid the green ruler labels. MEASUREMENT CONVENTION. Each plate carries a slight scan rotation (Ave K centre drifts -0.0014 px/row on sheet 56, +0.0049 px/row on sheet 62), so each centreline was measured in seven y bands from y=600 to y=3400, fitted linearly and evaluated at the sheet's vertical mid-height y=1949. Reading instead in the bands adjacent to the shared 30TH ST seam gives 56 K=2196.5 / 62 K=2169.5, a shift of -27.0 rather than -21.9; that ~5 px is the honest uncertainty from the opposed tilts.
